sourceConclusions: The optional host port is the only new adapter entry. Absent-port legacy prefix behavior stays explicit; this target does not enable runtime/factory/client exports.

Whole immutable bytes and the fixed ownership/event-id/sequence plan are written and fsynced before body transmission. Recovery uses that plan and retained ACK/unknown facts, without invoking a provider or creating an attempt.

The single outbox tail/body barrier serializes complete material and finalization. The c86 persist-poison delta includes initial ordinary persistence failures in the existing failure authority, preventing a later body from overtaking an unpersisted event.

8MiB per body, 16MiB per attempt, 256 bodies, 64KiB chunks, at most eight events per body batch and four chunks per read page are enforced; original total 2MiB event-batch schema remains applied. These are not aggregate runner memory/disk guarantees.

Ingestion reuses runner-share/task/attempt ownership locks and the original report transaction/fence, binds immutable activity/session/attempt, verifies chunk continuity and full SHA on seal. Shared applyEvent makes both ordinary and steering finalization reject incomplete body state.

Reader uses the original owner/browser role hook when mounted, task-bound activity identity, readonly repeatable-read transaction, bounded pages and content digests. Legacy means no complete protocol body is retained; complete material is not tool success.

The three prepared database scenarios exercise real HTTP plus explicit module migration/routes, not the default factory. Their fixture checkpoint/marker/connection/deadline/normal-drop safeguards were read; actual outer run supervision and fresh permit remain prerequisites.
